subject: Continuous batching & budget: post-demo qualification (FintechX)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@fintechx.com>, Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@fintechx.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-02-11T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Continuous batching & budget: post-demo qualification (FintechX)

Hi Elaine / Bryan — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can scope a concise POC and cost quote.

Recap of what we heard (please correct any of this):
- Expected token volume: ~0.8 - 1.2M tokens/day (roughly 24 - 36M/month) for the pilot.
- Traffic shape: primarily synchronous user queries; peak burst QPS up to ~45 for short periods, sustained concurrent active requests typically 6-10.
- Mix: ~60% short queries (<64 tokens), ~30% mid-length (64-512), ~10% long generation (>1024).
- Latency requirement: 95th under 350ms for short queries; 99th under 700ms for mixed workloads.
- Budget target: you mentioned a target of ~$18 / 1M tokens but indicated flexibility up to ~$28 if SLAs and latency are guaranteed.

Batching & concurrency assumptions we discussed:
- We expect to use continuous batching with a small batching window (30-50ms) to keep p95 low while aggregating requests.
- Suggested concurrency cap for the POC: 8 concurrent streams per model replica initially.
- KV/prefix caching expected to help for repeated prompts (you estimated ~25-40% repeat rate).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the 0.8-1.2M tokens/day band and the % split across short/mid/long?
2) Please share a 48-hour sample traffic CSV (timestamped requests, request token length, generation token length) — that will let us run a realistic cost simulation.
3) We'll attach an initial cost model and a POC scope doc; please confirm if the $18/1M target is a firm goal for the pilot or just a directional number.

Attachments: redwood-batching-cost-model.xlsx (cost model, initial assumptions)

If that matches your expectations I’ll loop in Lauren and Monica to size the infra and produce a pilot SOW.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com

From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@fintechx.com>

Date: 2026-02-12T10:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Continuous batching & budget: post-demo qualification (FintechX)

Thanks Sean — great summary. A few confirmations and clarifications from our side:

- Volume: pilot expected to generate ~0.9 - 1.1M tokens/day (so your 24-36M/mo is right in the ballpark). The team prefers that you size for the high end (1.1M/day) for estimates.
- Mix: we'll profile with roughly 55% short (<64), 35% mid (64-512), 10% long (>1024). Long jobs are often scheduled by a small subset of power users.
- Latency & budget: our procurement lead is targeting $18 / 1M tokens as a negotiating target, but if you can show consistent p95/p99 under the latency numbers above and offer a capped pilot spend we can stretch to $25-28.
- Concurrency: our app opens a websocket per user; expect steady-state concurrency around 8-12, with short spikes to 40-50 during batch ingest windows.

We will:
- Share the 48-hour sample traffic CSV by EOD Friday (I’ll send through Bryan).
- Confirm whether we need an NDA (we already have a standing NDA with several vendors; I’ll check and get back).

For the POC scope: please include an explicit line item for continuous batching behavior (batch window configurable), a fallback variant (lower-cost quantized model) for extreme bursts, and a simple dashboard for token spend vs. SLOs.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Wu
Head of Product (Platform) | FintechX
elaine.wu@fintechx.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-02-13T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Continuous batching & budget: post-demo qualification (FintechX)

Quick internal note / proposal for the POC sizing based on the confirmed profile:

Assumptions we should use for the POC cost model:
- Target daily tokens: 1.1M/day (peak sizing).
- Request distribution: 55% short / 35% mid / 10% long.
- Concurrency: configure pool with concurrency cap = 10; autoscale threshold at 80% utilization.
- Continuous batching policy: target batch window = 40ms (configurable), max batch size 128 requests; idle flush at 45ms.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 350ms (short), p99 < 700ms (mixed).

Suggested infra for pilot:
- 2 x GPU replicas (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) with dynamic batching enabled + prefix/KV cache (expected 30-40% token reduction on repeat flows).
- Fallback path: a quantized variant (8-bit) for burst overflow; route policy to fall back after queue depth > 3s.

Cost bands to present in the quote:
- Band A (target): $18 / 1M tokens — includes standard caching & continuous batching config, no SLA credits.
- Band B (premium): $25 / 1M tokens — includes 99th latency SLO, priority routing, and 24/7 on-call.
- Pilot fixed fee estimate: 30-day pilot run ~ $1,800 - $2,400 (depends on caching hit rate).

I attached the initial cost model (redwood-batching-cost-model.xlsx) — Sean, happy to jump on a quick call with you and Elaine to walk line-by-line. Monica, please flag any operational constraints I’m missing (quota, burst pricing, logging retention).

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
